title: Even Mathematicians Are Rethinking the Job
hook: A Fields Medalist tells The Verge he's spent the past year 'soul searching' about his field's future — a snapshot of how AI unsettles even the most deliberate professions.
key_points: Oxford mathematician and Fields Medalist James Maynard describes a year of soul searching about the field.
The Verge frames mathematics as a traditionally slow-moving discipline now hurrying to adapt.
Math is unusually exposed: proofs are symbolic, and correctness can be checked.
Verification is the anchor — a machine-written proof is a claim until humans check it.
The pattern generalizes: AI arrives first where work is formal, textual, and checkable.
content_html: James Maynard, an Oxford professor and Fields Medal winner, told The Verge he's spent much of the past year "soul searching" about the future of his field. The piece describes mathematics — a discipline that usually moves on a scale of decades — scrambling to work out what AI means for it.
extra_html:
Math is a revealing early case rather than a special one. Its output is symbolic text, and crucially, correctness can be checked: a proof either holds up under scrutiny or it doesn't. That combination is exactly where AI systems land first, and it's why generated proofs have already produced striking results.

It's also why the profession isn't simply being replaced. A machine-written proof is a claim until mathematicians verify it step by step — and as generation gets cheaper, verification becomes the scarce, valuable work. That's the part worth carrying into your own field: the tasks under pressure are the formal, text-shaped, checkable ones, and the human role tends to shift from producing the draft to judging whether the draft is right.

related.title: An AI Cracked an 80-Year-Old Math Problem
related.hook: An OpenAI model produced a solution to a famous math problem that had stumped people for about 80 years — a real milestone, with some important fine print.

related.title: AI & Jobs
related.hook: AI is less likely to take your whole job than to take certain tasks within it. The pattern through history: tools reshape work faster than they erase it.

related.title: Future-Proofing Your Career
related.hook: You won't be replaced by AI so much as by a person who uses it well. The hedge isn't out-typing the machine — it's getting fluent with it while doubling down on what's stubbornly human.

flashcards.prompt: Why is mathematics an unusually early test case for AI changing a profession?

choices.text: Its work is symbolic and its answers can be checked, so machine output is verifiable
Mathematicians were the first to adopt computers
Math requires no creativity, only calculation

flashcards.explanation_html: AI lands earliest where the output is formal text and there's a way to confirm whether it's right — which is exactly the shape of a proof.

flashcards.prompt: What keeps a machine-generated proof from settling a question on its own?
flashcards.back_html: It's a claim until human mathematicians verify each step. Verification is what converts generated output into an accepted result.

flashcards.prompt: What's the transferable lesson for other kinds of work?

choices.text: Formal, text-based, checkable work feels AI pressure first — and judgment shifts toward verifying
Every profession will be automated at the same pace
Only manual labor is safe from AI

flashcards.explanation_html: As generation gets cheap, the scarce human skill moves toward deciding whether what was generated is actually correct and worth using.
